title: The 10 Best Cordless Jigsaws
subtitle: Battery-powered jigsaws ranked from live Amazon data — best-sellers, real ratings, honest trade-offs.
intro: A jigsaw is the tool for curves, cutouts, and plunge cuts a circular saw can't make, and a cordless one goes wherever the cut needs to happen. Most of the best-sellers here ship as a bare tool with no battery, so check whether a pick is tool-only or a ready-to-use kit, and which battery platform it rides. Blade speed, orbital action, and bevel range vary more than you'd expect across brands — the buyer's guide below breaks down what each one actually changes about your cut.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Jig Saw, 3,200 Blade Speed, Cordless, Brushless Motor, LED Light, Bare Tool Only (DCS334B)

Bare tool, so budget for a 20V MAX battery.
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V MAX owners who want the best all-round jigsaw.
products.skip_if: You don't own DEWALT batteries and want one box with everything.
pros: 9,683 reviews at 4.8 stars — more than any other jigsaw here, with 3,000+ bought in the past month
Brushless motor rated for longer runtime than DEWALT's own DCS331
All-metal keyless blade change and keyless bevel adjustment (0°/15°/30°/45°)
cons: Bare tool — no battery or charger included
Compact-grip body trades some leverage versus the barrel-grip DCS335B

products.verdict: The cheapest way onto this list: a $30.99 bare jigsaw built to run on DEWALT 20V MAX batteries, with 3 orbital settings, a 45° bevel both ways and a keyless lever blade clamp. avoid.name: CAMXTOOL Cordless Jig Saw Compatible with Dewalt 20V Max Battery (No Battery), Brushless, LED Light
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on orbital settings and bevel
avoid.verdict: An unbranded DEWALT-battery clone whose own listing can't agree on how it works. The EMTMOUN EM-JS-01 on this page fits the same batteries for $9 less with a listing that agrees with itself, and the BLACK+DECKER BDCJS20C kit comes with its battery and charger.
reasons: The title says '3 Orbital Settings'; the bullet points say '4-position orbital action.' One of them is wrong, and the listing doesn't say which.
The title gives the bevel as '0°- 45°', while the bullets say the shoe tilts 45° left or right. Those are different saws.
Speed is listed as '0-2800RPM'. Jigsaws are rated in strokes per minute, and this listing never gives one, so it can't be compared with the 3,200 SPM DEWALT DCS334B on this page.
It's a third-party body made to fit DEWALT 20V batteries. DEWALT doesn't make or warrant it.

buyers_guide.a: A bare tool ships with no battery or charger — worth it if you already own the brand's batteries, a dead end if you don't. A kit includes a battery and charger and sometimes blades, ready to cut out of the box. Each pick above says which.

buyers_guide.q: What does orbital action actually do?
buyers_guide.a: Orbital action moves the blade slightly forward on the upstroke in addition to up-and-down, which speeds up cutting in soft materials like wood at the cost of a rougher edge. Dial it down (or off) for clean cuts in metal, plastic, or finished surfaces, and up for fast, aggressive cuts in framing lumber.

buyers_guide.q: How many strokes per minute (SPM) do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Most cordless jigsaws run 2,500-3,200 SPM at full speed, which covers wood, plastic, and thin metal. Variable-speed triggers let you slow down for tight curves or delicate materials, so the max number matters less than having good low-end control.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and hold speed better under load — worth it if you'll use the saw often or push it through thick material. For occasional cuts around the house, a brushed tool like the CRAFTSMAN or BLACK+DECKER picks is fine.

buyers_guide.q: Which battery platform should I buy into?
buyers_guide.a: Buy on the same platform as tools you already own (DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18, Makita 18V LXT, CRAFTSMAN V20) so one battery lineup covers everything. If you own nothing yet, a self-contained kit like the BLACK+DECKER, SEESII, or WOODERS avoids the platform lock-in.

T-shank is the modern standard and what most tool-free blade clamps are designed around — it's what you'll find on hardware store shelves. A saw that accepts both T and U shank blades, like the CRAFTSMAN picks, gives you more flexibility if you're using older or off-brand blades.
